1.explanation:
• DataTable/DataTable.mdx – shows the general API and describes props like expandHeader and sortable headers.
• DataTable/migrate-to-7.x.md – explains any recent changes to DataTable/TableHeader in v7 that could affect prop spreading.
• DataTable/state/ – contains the stateful example of sorting behavior and TableHeader usage for sortable columns.
• DataTable/stories/expansion/ – demonstrates the expandHeader pattern and accessible header cells (related to ARIA attributes and ids).
• DataTable/stories/dynamic-content/ – shows a non-sortable table where ...rest lands on <th>, illustrating the contrast with sortable headers.

Together these documents provide the context, usage examples, and code patterns needed to understand where TableHeader’s prop spreading is intended and how to reproduce the mismatch in your own code.
1.bug_scenario: When using the DataTable component’s TableHeader in carbon-components-react v7.48.0, you can pass arbitrary props (via the ...rest spread) onto the <th> for non-sortable columns, but for sortable columns those same props end up on the inner <button> instead of the <th>. In practice this means you cannot set things like an id on the <th> of a sortable column—which breaks the WCAG H43 requirement for associating header cells to their content.
